title: Grothendieck's existence theorem for coherent modules with support proper over a complete Noetherian ring
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal such that $A$ is $I$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $S_n=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I^{n+1})$ ($n\ge0$), let $X\to S$ be separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] and of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $X_n=X\times_SS_n$ [def-pc-base-change], $i_n:X_n\to X_{n+1}$ and $j_n:X_n\to X$ the closed immersions, and for an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G$ write $\mathcal G|_{X_n}=j_n^*\mathcal G$ [def-pc-module-pullback], with the canonical isomorphisms $c_n:i_n^*(\mathcal G|_{X_{n+1}})\cong\mathcal G|_{X_n}$ (from $j_{n+1}\circ i_n=j_n$). Coherent modules are as in [pqf-def-coherent], support proper over a base as in [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base]. (a) (Full faithfulness.) If $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ are coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules with support proper over $S$, then the map $u\mapsto(u|_{X_n})_{n\ge0}$ is a bijection from $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal G,\mathcal F)$ onto the set of families $(u_n:\mathcal G|_{X_n}\to\mathcal F|_{X_n})_{n\ge0}$ of $\mathcal O_{X_n}$-linear maps with $u_n\circ c_n=c_n\circ i_n^*u_{n+1}$ for all $n$. (b) (Existence.) Let $(\mathcal F_n,\varphi_n)_{n\ge0}$ be a system of coherent $\mathcal O_{X_n}$-modules $\mathcal F_n$ and isomorphisms $\varphi_n:i_n^*\mathcal F_{n+1}\to\mathcal F_n$ such that $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F_0)$ is proper over $S_0$ (for $X_0\to S_0$). Then there are a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ with support proper over $S$ and isomorphisms $\psi_n:\mathcal F|_{X_n}\to\mathcal F_n$ with $\varphi_n\circ i_n^*\psi_{n+1}=\psi_n\circ c_n$ for all $n$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Theorem 088E (theorem-grothendieck-existence: the functor (088D, equation-completion-functor-proper-over-A) Coh_{support proper over A}(O_X) -> Coh_{support proper over A}(X, I) is an equivalence) in the form of Remark 088F (remark-reformulate-existence-theorem); Stacks indexes S_n = Spec(A/I^n), n >= 1, here shifted by one. EGA III_1 Theorem 5.1.5 is Stacks' reference

proof.text: Finite type over the Noetherian affine base supplies an IsNoetherian structure on $X$ [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft]. Use [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] to equip each coherent module with quasi-coherent and finite-type instances. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-support-proper-over-base] to obtain proper closed subschemes $Z_F,Z_G$ whose ideals annihilate the two modules.

Construct $K=\mathcal I_{Z_F}\mathcal I_{Z_G}$ and its canonical closed subscheme. Mathlib IdealSheafData.support_mul identifies its support with the union of the two kernel supports; Hom.support_ker and closedness identify these with the ranges. [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-union-preimage] makes this union proper; [lem-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base-properties] transfers properness to the constructed subscheme. The product ideal is contained in both ideals. Use the existing upstream Scheme.IdealSheafData.idealOfOpens_mono from Curve.DivisorIdealSheaf for monotonicity on arbitrary-open sections. Hence K kills both modules.

Use [lem-weil-pbc-grothendieck-existence-supported-hom] on this common proper closed subscheme. Surjectivity gives a morphism lifting the given compatible family. Evaluate its subtype equality at each index to prove the desired restriction equations. Injectivity, subtype extensionality and function extensionality show that any other such lift equals it.

For a coherent system with proper first support, [lem-weil-pbc-grothendieck-existence-system-support] gives a proper closed subscheme annihilating all the pushed terms. Supply this subscheme, its closed-immersion and properness instances, and its annihilation equations to [lem-weil-pbc-grothendieck-existence-supported-system]. Its conclusion is exactly the algebraization and the compatible restriction isomorphisms required.

proof_origin.place: Theorem 088E, first paragraph (proper closed supports), and Remark 088F. The common annihilating subscheme is explicitly constructed from the product ideal, which has the same union support as the intersection ideal in the former plan. The three remaining transport/support arguments are named intermediate nodes; existence and uniqueness are combined in Lean.

reviewed.note: Reviewed by the lead (opus-relaunch6). Ten steps along the proof of 088E in the form of 088F; fifteen new unsplit nodes, statements checked against coherent.tex: the definition of Coh(X,I), the completion functor and the proper-support subcategories (0EHN/0880/088D); the dictionary between systems on the X_n and Coh(X,I) (088F, proof to be agent-written); 087T; 087X(1); 0CYV; 0883; 088C; 0885 for closed subschemes of P^n_A; 0887; 088B with the kernel/cokernel objects of 0888 (its statement includes the coherence of f_* G, Stacks 02O5, so lem-pc-coherent-hi of another unit is not cited; to be revisited when 088B is split: lem-pc-coherent-hi as a tool use); 0200 in the dense-open form (the Lean candidates ChowModification.nonempty_data / exists_dense_isIso_restrict, sorry-free with @[stacks 0200], are recorded on thm-chow-lemma and may be attached when that node is read against its Lean); 0CYJ; 01Y8; 056J; 0CYR/0CYQ(3). Full faithfulness via a common closed subscheme Z proper over S and 0883; essential surjectivity by Noetherian induction on the annihilator ideal, Chow's lemma with lem-chow-closed-model (closed Lean, tool) for the projective compactification, the projective case, the support argument through the Jacobson radical of the complete ring, the push-pull comparison and the Serre subcategory of systems with proper support. The implicit parts of Stacks (Supp F_n = Supp F_1, the system j_* f^* F_n, K^t nonzero) are written out.
